_comment: Each entry must name the exact case id, say why the difference is not a defect,
and classify it as spec-ambiguous or spec-unique-answer-{Rust,Python}-bug.
The file starts empty on purpose: the first gate 3 run must fail until every
difference is understood. A stale entry (its case now matches) also fails the gate.
H1-FIX1 (2026-11-14): the four F11 entries were removed; S14 fixed the input identity of a container without a manifest (both members null), so those reports are compared byte for byte again.

H1-FIX2 (2026-11-15, Y10): every entry names the report fields that may differ ('fields', paths with [*] for array positions; <exit-code>, <report>, <report-bytes> outside the JSON tree) and the script's reading of expected.json ('vector_basis'). The fields the script computes must equal the listed ones exactly, the basis must match, and the classification must be consistent with the basis (a Rust bug is never listed; rust-only-matches-expected requires spec-unique-answer-Python-bug; both-match-expected allows spec-unique-answer-Python-bug, citing the specification in 'reason', or spec-ambiguous).

H1-FIX2B (2026-11-15, Z3): field paths keep their array indices (records[3].sigs[0].state) instead of [*], and arrays of different lengths are compared element by element (an element on one side only is its own indexed path), so a regression in another element of an allow-listed array is a new path and fails the gate.

H1-S2 (2026-11-15, decision 2026-11-15 #20): the Rust verifier follows the S2 round and S2-FIX1 of revision 3; every report is identical byte for byte, so the 37 entries were removed and the list is empty again.
